incident-bot: PAGER: kv-cache fragmentation + continuous-batching errors detected on prod-cluster-usw2. error_rate=12% (5m) > pager_threshold. affected service: inference-runtime-2 (continuous-batching shards 3/8). suspected allocator churn (pytorch/cuda malloc warnings). runbook: #incidents->kv-frag.
Maya: ack, I'm up. pinging oncall. I can triage logs.
Rohit (oncall): taking pager. setting priority HIGH. Maya, can you pull the last 30m of kernel logs and nvml logs?
Dylan: grabbing nvml and dmesg now. seeing repeated "cuda runtime error: out of memory" + "pytorch.c10d: arena fragmentation" messages. sample:```
[2026-03-15T02:12:41Z] runtime: cudaMalloc returned OOM (alloc 256MB)
[2026-03-15T02:12:41Z] torch: Arena allocator fragmentation: large free list miss, fallback to malloc
[2026-03-15T02:12:42Z] kv_cache: slab_util=92% active_slots dropping, continuous_batch queue depth spiked
```
Maya: that's consistent with KV cache blowups we've seen when cont-batching ramps up with long sequences.
Rohit (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle continuous batching globally 2) trigger kv compaction on affected nodes 3) if noise persists, disable cont-batching for canary pool.
Jen: +1. how to throttle quickly?
Rohit (oncall): deploying hotfix to runtime config. patch: set CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=1024 and CONT_BATCH_INTERVAL_MS=15, and reduce CONT_BATCH_PARALLELISM=4 for canary pool. Deploy-bot will push.
deploy-bot: rolling config update to inference-runtime-2/canary: CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=1024, CONT_BATCH_PARALLELISM=4, CONT_BATCH_INTERVAL_MS=15. 8 nodes targeted, sequential rolling. ETA ~ 90s per node.
Ella: while that rolls, I'll trigger on-demand KV compaction on the worst 3 nodes (ids: i-0a1b2c3d, i-0f1e2d3c, i-09a8b7c6). command:```
rdctl infra kv compact --cluster prod-cluster-usw2 --nodes i-0a1b2c3d,i-0f1e2d3c,i-09a8b7c6 --force
```
Dylan: compaction jobs started. logs show immediate free-slab reclamation on i-0a1b2c3d. slab_util dropped 92% -> 48% within 20s.
Amy (CS): FYI we have 3 customer tickets flagging latency spikes and intermittent 500s (AcmeCorp, BetaApp, HealthFlow). Any ETA on impact reduction?
Rohit (oncall): tentatively 10-15m after compaction + config roll. I'll update status page once we confirm. Amy, please post to status page: degraded performance, ongoing mitigation.
Amy (CS): posting now. message: "We are investigating increased latency for inference requests in US-WEST-2. Engineers are mitigating; no data loss. Updates within 30 minutes."
Luca (product): are there traffic routing options? Can we shift some traffic to eu-west to reduce customer impact?
Jen: we can bleed non-SLA traffic to eu-west with routing policy, but that adds cross-region latency. I'd rather stabilize first.
Rohit (oncall): agree. hold redirect for now. update: deploy-bot finished rolling config to 6/8 nodes; 2 nodes remaining (one failed to drain).
deploy-bot: failed to drain node i-0f1e2d3c: pod stuck terminating (mount in use). retrying with force-evict.
Maya: note — during retry we saw a spike in allocation failures on that node. suspect process leak holding GPU memory. I'm going to ssh and inspect cgroups.
Dylan: evidence of runaway prefetcher process on i-0f1e2d3c pinned ~11GB GPU memory despite low request rate. killing that process freed memory and allowed drain.
Rohit (oncall): config roll now complete 8/8. monitoring: error_rate down to 2.1% (5m), latency p95 improved from 1.8s -> 650ms for canary.
Ella: compaction completed for all targeted nodes. cluster slab_util avg dropped 88% -> 46%. nvml shows stabilized allocations.
Amy (CS): tickets updated, customers notified. AcmeCorp responding: "thanks, seeing improvements on our end".
Luca (product): OK good. we should schedule a canary with traffic replay to validate perf cliff fixes.
Maya: creating a short replay job + synthetic long-seq load to validate cont-batching settings.
Rohit (oncall): next steps for oncall wrap: 1) temporary run with tightened batch settings for 24h, 2) schedule eng-runtime deep-dive to investigate allocator fragmentation root cause (likely allocator changes in last runtime patch), 3) prepare rollback plan for cont-batching feature if we see recurrence. Assigning to Dylan + Maya.
Jen: adding infra-owner Ella for arena tuning and pytorch malloc flags. Suggest enabling TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.7 or trying arena_max_split_size to reduce fragmentation.
Dylan: noted. capturing stack traces for suspect processes and saving nvprof traces.
Maya: will open postmortem ticket with timeline, customers impacted, and proposed remedial changes (allocator tuning + cont-batch backpressure).
Rohit (oncall): handing off to Jen for overnight oncall. Jen, you're oncall for the next shift. I'll brief in #oncall-handoff.
Jen: taking over. thanks Rohit. please drop any artifacts in the incident doc.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: kv-frag-contbatch-oom-2159876543 acknowledged. status: mitigated->stabilizing. severity: SEV2.
Maya: note for postmortem: allocate follow-ups — runtime rollback test, improved canary gating on allocator metrics, and KV compaction as a safety trigger when slab_util > 80%.
Amy (CS): I'll follow up with customers for any residual degradation.
Rohit (oncall): great work team. ending live thread.
